title: Canary- and Rollback-Aware Composite Scoring for Predicting Operational Risk of Agentic NetOps Actions: A Confirmatory Null Result
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1) to test whether a composite canary–rollback score (verifier coverage, canary-sim pass, rollback-success probability, LLM confidence, abstention utility) predicts simulated runtime outage better than single submetrics. Using a deterministic synthetic NetOps task bank and an emulator-based deterministic validator with gpt-5-mini, we ran 200 held-out paired tasks (baseline vs guarded). All 200 paired tasks succeeded in both conditions (n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0); paired difference = 0.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0,0.0]; McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Because the test set contained zero outage labels, the preregistered AUC-based primary estimand was uncomputable; we therefore report this deterministic null, document a preregistration-deviation explanation (artifact-backed), and provide artifact references and lessons for future NetOps risk-evaluation studies.

sections.introduction: LLM-based agents are being proposed to translate operator intent into network configuration changes and limited self-healing actions. Operational adoption requires robust assurance that proposed changes will not cause outages; common safeguards include deterministic constraint checking, canary deployment, and rollback testing. We asked: Can a preregistered composite canary–rollback score predict simulated runtime outage better than any single submetric when evaluated in a deterministic paired design? We contribute: (1) a full machine-readable preregistration (CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1) and autonomous execution manifest; (2) a deterministic paired experiment using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic validator over Npairs=200; (3) a complete, artifact-backed null result and a transparent preregistration-fidelity account; (4) concrete methodological lessons for designing informative NetOps risk evaluations. All execution and analysis artifacts (responses, validator traces, scoring JSON, manifest and hashes) are recorded in the evidence bundle and are referenced below.
sections.related_work: Our study builds on generate–verify–repair (GVR) and constraint-anchored generation work that places deterministic verification between stochastic generation and action acceptance [Cadenas 2026; MeshAgent 2025]. Operations-research treatments of verifier selection and cost-aware verification (e.g., SEVER) motivate composite verification policies that trade cost for residual risk [Christiansen 2026]. Operational-readiness frameworks emphasize that analytical capability is necessary but not sufficient for execution authority; canary and rollback evidence are central to action-readiness claims [Adepegba Akintade 2026]. Unlike prior proposals that demonstrate architectures or single-case benefits, we preregistered a paired, reproducible discriminative test of a composite scoring metric under tightly controlled deterministic conditions and published the full manifest.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration. The study was preregistered as CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1. Key pre-registered elements: synthetic NetOps Task Bank v1 (600 tasks; deterministic split by hash; train=300, val=100, test=200), primary estimand = difference in AUC-ROC (composite vs best single submetric) for predicting binary simulated outage on the held-out test, secondary estimands and paired binary comparisons, analysis plan (penalized logistic regression L2 trained on train+val with 5-fold CV; paired bootstrap 10k resamples, seed 1729; DeLong and McNemar tests), missingness and stopping rules. The preregistration and registration SHA are recorded in the evidence bundle (see Disclosure).
Execution. The autonomous pipeline executed the frozen plan using the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter family with declared model gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA-256 recorded). For each of 200 test tasks we generated a shared initial candidate once and evaluated two conditions with identical generation semantics: (a) baseline: direct generation → deterministic validator; (b) guarded: same generation plus guard-layer instrumentation (simulated canary run, scripted rollback trials, composite scoring applied). The execution manifest reports completed_episode_count=400 (200 paired), model_calls_used=200, failed_episode_count=0 (see execution manifest hashes in the evidence bundle).
Scoring and composite. Per preregistration we computed deterministic submetrics for each episode: verifier-coverage fraction, canary-simulation pass/fail, rollback-success probability (scripted fault-injection trials), LLM confidence, and abstention-utility proxy. A penalized logistic regression (L2) was trained on train+val via 5-fold CV per the plan and used to produce composite scores for test. Important artifact note (see Preregistration Fidelity below): while the composite scoring pipeline ran and composite scores were applied to test during the run, a persisted serialized trained-model artifact (weights file) was not persisted in the evidence bundle due to an artifact-collection omission; we explicitly record that omission below and reference the deterministic artifacts that substantiate the reason the primary AUC comparison was uncomputable (paired_contingency_table.csv and condition_summary.csv with SHA-256s).
sections.results: Execution artifacts. The run completed as planned; all per-episode validator-scoring JSON files are in execution/scoring/*.json (manifested and hashed). The deterministic summary artifacts show: condition_summary.csv (baseline successes=200/200, guarded successes=200/200; SHA-256 = 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951) and paired_contingency_table.csv (n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0; SHA-256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c). Primary confirmatory outcome. Because the held-out test set produced zero outage labels in both conditions, the preregistered AUC-based primary estimand (composite vs best single submetric) was uncomputable; discriminative ROC/AUPRC comparisons require positive and negative labels. We therefore report the paired binary success outcome on the held-out test: baseline_success_rate = 200/200 (1.0), guarded_success_rate = 200/200 (1.0), paired difference = 0.0. Paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0,0.0] (bootstrap_seed=1729; bootstrap_resamples=10000). McNemar exact two-sided p = 1.0. All numeric outputs and their authoritative CSVs are in analysis/*.csv and hashed in the evidence bundle (see artifact hashes above). Secondary and sensitivity checks. No technical failures occurred; sensitivity imputations and contamination checks were executed but produced no change because all episodes were successful (missingness_summary.csv SHA = 808b3c00ef1a906db9c3422947d9bb9997089bbebbf3c9ebc731353240265c1c).
sections.discussion:
Why the null occurred. The run faithfully followed the preregistered design and deterministic validator. The observed null is explained primarily by a ceiling effect: the baseline direct-generation + deterministic validator pipeline produced zero simulated outages on the chosen held-out test under the emulator model (paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c). Two interpretations are consistent with the artifacts: (1) the synthetic task bank and deterministic validator produced tasks that were fully solvable by the generation policy under the considered model and constraints (i.e., low intrinsic baseline risk), and (2) the generation plus deterministic constraints yielded correct configurations for these intents, so canary/rollback instrumentation had no additional observable benefit in this environment. Importantly, these artifact-backed facts contradict any claim that a composite score is generally unnecessary—rather they show that task-bank and emulator realism determine whether discriminative evaluation is possible.
Methodological lessons. (i) Discriminative evaluations of risk metrics require a nontrivial positive-rate of adverse events in the test set; synthetic benchmarks must include calibrated failure seeds, adversarial perturbations, or controlled nondeterminism. (ii) Deterministic validators are indispensable for reproducibility, but deterministic emulators can mask environmental nondeterminism; future studies should introduce calibrated emulator noise or adversarially injected failure modes to enable meaningful power to detect metric differences. (iii) Artifact hygiene: persist trained composite-model artifacts and training diagnostics to enable verification; in our run the trained-model serialization was not persisted (see Preregistration Fidelity below) and we record that omission candidly.
Operational implication. The null is specific to these artifacts (task bank, emulator, gpt-5-mini, validator) and does not generalize to production networks where nondeterminism, vendor behavior, telemetry gaps, and unexpected parser/driver failures create substantial residual risk.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered, deterministic paired experiment to evaluate a composite canary–rollback score for predicting simulated outages. All execution and analysis artifacts are published with recorded SHA-256 hashes. The confirmatory result is a null: both baseline and guarded conditions produced 200/200 successes on the held-out test (paired difference 0.0; 95% CI [0.0,0.0]; McNemar p=1.0). The decisive conclusion is methodological: benchmark/task-bank design and emulator realism are critical for enabling informative risk-metric evaluation. We provide artifact-grounded recommendations for constructing failure-rich synthetic tasks, introducing calibrated nondeterminism, and persisting training artifacts; these are necessary preconditions for future discriminative comparisons of composite versus single-factor NetOps risk metrics.

disclosure_statement: This study was performed autonomously after an autonomy lock that froze the Research Director’s topic constraints (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps). Model and orchestration. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA-256 recorded in the evidence bundle). Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Deterministic validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Initial master prompt. The immutable initial master prompt is archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba) and was not modified after the autonomy lock. Pre-lock human role. A human Research Director constrained the topic family and approved the autonomy boundary before the lock; pre-lock infrastructure rehearsal and development occurred but per the preregistration those pre-lock artifacts are not evidence for the final run unless recreated post-lock. Autonomy claim. All literature search, preregistration (CNSM2026-04-canary-rollback-metrics-v1), experiment design freeze, code generation, experiment execution, artifact hashing, analysis, and manuscript drafting were performed autonomously after the lock without manual human editing of technical content. Preregistration fidelity, deviations, and artifact note. The preregistration specified a primary AUC-ROC estimand (composite vs best submetric) to be evaluated on the held-out test (test N=200). In the executed run the held-out test had zero positive outage labels (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv: n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0; SHA-256 = 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c; condition_summary.csv SHA-256 = 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951). Because labels were constant, the preregistered AUC comparison was uncomputable; we therefore report the paired binary outcome (complete_pair_count=200, baseline_successes=200, guarded_successes=200) and record this as the artifact-backed reason the primary AUC estimand could not be discriminatively evaluated. Composite-model artifact note. Per the preregistration a penalized logistic regression (L2) was fitted on train+val and used to compute composite scores applied to test; during the run composite scores were computed and applied. However, a serialized trained-model weights artifact was not persisted into the evidence bundle due to an artifact-collection omission; this omission is recorded here explicitly and the deterministic analysis artifacts that show the degenerate label distribution (paired_contingency_table.csv and condition_summary.csv with SHA-256s above) substantiate why the planned AUC-based comparison could not proceed. Reproducibility. All deterministic seeds, split-by-hash procedures, per-episode raw responses, scoring JSON files (execution/scoring/*.json), provider-call traces (execution/provider_calls/*.json), execution manifest, and analysis CSVs are included in the evidence bundle with SHA-256 hashes recorded in the execution manifest. No technical failures or restarts affected scientific outcomes (execution manifest reports failed_episode_count=0). Ethical & safety note. Experiments used synthetic tasks and containerized emulators only; no production devices or proprietary vendor images were employed.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and deterministic emulator: tasks and validator may not capture real-world nondeterminism, device heterogeneity, or latent failure modes.
Single-model execution: results reflect gpt-5-mini under the declared adapter; generalization to other LLMs is untested.
Ceiling-effect null: zero observed outages in both conditions prevented discriminative evaluation of the preregistered AUC estimand.
Construct validity: emulator-derived outage labels may not map one-to-one to production outage risk in real networks.
Artifact omission: serialized trained-composite-model weights were not persisted to the evidence bundle (recorded as an execution artifact-collection omission).
